actions.justification: MANDATORY: Immediate stroke team activation is critical at time 0. Patient presents with classic stroke symptoms (left-sided weakness, facial droop) within the tPA treatment window. Coordinated stroke team response is essential to meet the 60-minute door-to-needle time target.
MANDATORY: IV access must be established immediately for potential tPA administration, blood draws, and IV fluids. This is a prerequisite for any IV therapy in this acute stroke patient.

MANDATORY: Patient has an irregularly irregular pulse strongly suggesting atrial fibrillation, which is a major cardioembolic source for ischemic stroke. 12-lead ECG is critical to confirm AFib, assess for other cardiac pathology, and inform anticoagulation decisions relevant to tPA eligibility.

Serial vital sign assessment is critical in acute stroke. BP must be monitored closely — tPA requires BP <185/110 mmHg. Current BP 172/96 is acceptable but trending is essential. SpO2 at 95% needs reassessment.

SpO2 is 95%, which is at the lower threshold. AHA stroke guidelines recommend supplemental oxygen if SpO2 <94%. Administering oxygen now is appropriate to optimize cerebral oxygenation in acute ischemic stroke.

12-lead ECG was already obtained. Patient has irregularly irregular pulse, highly suggestive of atrial fibrillation, which is the most likely cardioembolic source. Interpreting the ECG confirms AF, informs anticoagulation status assessment (critical for tPA eligibility), and guides acute management.

Patient has irregularly irregular pulse (likely AF) as the probable cardioembolic source of ischemic stroke. Troponin helps evaluate for concurrent ACS/cardioembolic etiology and guides management decisions.
Irregularly irregular pulse strongly suggests atrial fibrillation as the cardioembolic source. Cardiology input is needed for anticoagulation timing decisions post-stroke and AF management.

AHA guidelines recommend aspirin (325mg loading dose) for acute ischemic stroke. With CT head ordered to rule out hemorrhage and tPA eligibility being evaluated, aspirin initiation is appropriate per stroke protocol for acute ischemic stroke management.

Patient has AFib (irregularly irregular pulse) as likely cardioembolic source of stroke. Anticoagulation status must be reviewed per AHA stroke guidelines as part of tPA eligibility checklist. Prior anticoagulation use is a contraindication to tPA. This action addresses the critical guideline requirement to 'review_anticoagulation_status' before alteplase administration.

Obtaining additional history is needed to complete the tPA exclusion checklist - specifically to rule out recent surgery, active bleeding, or other contraindications. This aligns with AHA stroke guideline requirement to review exclusion criteria before tPA administration.

Patient has irregularly irregular pulse consistent with atrial fibrillation as the likely cardioembolic source of stroke. Comparing to prior ECG determines if AF is new-onset (requiring urgent rate control and anticoagulation planning) vs. chronic, directly guiding stroke management and anticoagulation decisions within the tPA eligibility window.

Patient has SpO2 of 95% and elevated BP; maintaining IV access and fluid status supports stroke management while awaiting CT results. This is one of the available actions relevant to supportive care in acute stroke.

NIHSS score quantifies stroke severity, guides tPA eligibility and thrombectomy candidacy, and is required per AHA stroke guidelines before treatment decisions. Patient is at 65 minutes — time-critical.

BP is 172/96 mmHg. tPA requires BP <185/110 mmHg before administration. Nitrates may be considered to optimize BP control approaching tPA eligibility threshold, though BP is currently below the absolute cutoff.

Non-contrast CT head is critical to rule out hemorrhage before any thrombolysis consideration. At 75 minutes, this is urgently needed per AHA stroke guidelines (deadline 25 min from arrival - must be done immediately).
Last known well time is essential to determine tPA eligibility window (4.5 hours from symptom onset). This directly affects treatment decisions for this acute ischemic stroke patient.

CTA of head and neck is indicated to evaluate for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and assess thrombectomy candidacy. Patient has acute ischemic stroke with suspected cardioembolic etiology (irregularly irregular pulse suggesting AF). CTA will guide endovascular therapy decisions if tPA is contraindicated or insufficient.

MRI DWI can confirm ischemic stroke, delineate infarct core and penumbra, and help determine stroke etiology and extent. Useful if CT head was non-diagnostic or to better characterize the ischemic territory prior to treatment decisions.

Glucose check is critical to rule out hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic. Per AHA stroke guidelines, check_glucose is a time-critical action within first 10 minutes. Not yet completed and essential before tPA consideration.

PT/INR and PTT are required before tPA eligibility can be confirmed. Patient has irregularly irregular pulse suggesting atrial fibrillation and may be on anticoagulation. Must check coagulation status to rule out contraindications to thrombolysis per AHA stroke guidelines.

CBC with platelet count is required as part of tPA eligibility checklist per AHA stroke guidelines. Thrombocytopenia (<100,000) is a contraindication to IV alteplase. This has not yet been completed and is needed before tPA administration.

Patient presents with acute ischemic stroke at 105 minutes since arrival, well within the 4.5-hour tPA window. BP is 172/96 mmHg (below the 185/110 threshold). CT head ordered to rule out hemorrhage, glucose checked, coagulation labs obtained. Per AHA stroke guidelines, IV alteplase is strongly recommended for eligible patients within the treatment window after exclusion of contraindications. Time is brain — door-to-needle goal is 60 minutes and this is already at 105 minutes.

Neurology consultation is critical at 115 minutes post-arrival for acute ischemic stroke. The patient has received tPA and needs neurology specialist involvement to guide ongoing management, assess response to thrombolysis, and evaluate candidacy for mechanical thrombectomy given the presentation with AF and significant neurological deficits.
